newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: NSW THROWS WEIGHT BEHIND LIVING WAGE CLAIM
The New South Wales Government has thrown its support behind the ACTU's living wage claim, saying it will ensure maintenance of the award system.
The Government argues that coalition governments have failed to note the role of awards in the Federal Workplace Relations Act.
The Labor Government has said the establishment of a proper award safety net is vital to maintaining a fair labour market, as required by the Workplace Relations Act.
Counsel Brendam Docking told the Full Bench of the Industrial Relations Commission, the enterprise bargaining system being pushed by the Government doesn't deliver fairly in all circumstances.
INFORMATION ON WOMEN AND VIOLENCE USEFUL TO POLICY MAKERS
The Head of the Office of the Status of Women, Kathy Townsend, says information from a report on violence against women released today, will be useful to those making public policy in the area.
The survey, commissioned by the Office from the Bureau of Statistics, shows more than seven per cent of women aged over 18 had experienced an incident of violence in the past 12 months.
Ms Townsend says many children are also exposed to violence in the home, and only 15 per cent of women reported violence to Police.
Ms Townsend says Commonwealth and State policy makers, such as Justice Departments, Police and Health Departments will be able to use the information in the report.
NO AGREEMENT YET ON DOCTOR NUMBERS
Negotiations are continuing between Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge and the Democrats over Government plans to reduce doctor numbers.
The move to restrict the annual number of Medicare Provider Numbers for new GP's has sparked industrial action today by junior doctors in New South Wales, the A-C-T and South Australia.
The Democrats want the impact of the cuts softened before they agree to support them in the Senate.
Doctor Wooldridge says he's willing to compromise and the Democrats' proposals are sensible but final agreement is yet to be reached.
NEW COMMANDER OF NORTHERN DEFENCE FORCE
A new commander has taken charge of the Australian Defence force Northern Command headquarters.

Brigadier Chris Roberts replaces Commodore John Lord at the Darwin-based headquarters which will oversee the defence of northern Australia, ranging from Cairns to the Pilbara district in Western Australia, from the middle of next year.
Brigadier Roberts has more than 30 years experience as a military officer with particular expertise in Special Forces, including Commanding officer of the Special Air Service Regiment.
The former Chief of Staff of the Army's Training Command was also responsible for planning and controlling Exercise Kangaroo 92.
